name: Infra-Bench Classification (Infra-Bench CLS) Imagery Dataset
description: Infra-Bench Classification (Infra-Bench CLS) pairs facility-scale critical-infrastructure assets identified in OpenStreetMap with co-located Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery, so that Earth-observation foundation models can be compared on a common classification task across seven continental regions and four infrastructure sectors. Each asset is represented by one 600m x 600m tile centred on its location, stacking seven Sentinel-2 L2A optical bands with the two Sentinel-1 RTC polarizations at 10m resolution. Labels are weak, in the sense that classes derive from OpenStreetMap tags rather than from manual inspection. The archive contains two parts. The benchmark comprises 28 "cells" named dataset_ _ _v1_1k, covering seven regions crossed with four sectors, each targeting 1,000 tiles drawn by proportional class-stratified sampling, for 18,756 tiles in total across a 13-class taxonomy. Additionally, the substation datasets, dataset_ _stac_v1, holds every deduplicated substation per region within the energy sector and without a per-cell cap. Each cell (e.g., Africa x energy) is a zip archive holding an images/ directory of .npy tiles, a manifest.json of per-tile metadata, and a summary.csv. Asset locations come from a Geofabrik OpenStreetMap snapshot dated 2026-05-26, and imagery from the Microsoft Planetary Computer, selecting the least-cloudy scene available for each asset within a 2021 to 2024 window.
